paper.title_en: Initial-state nuclear structure effects on dynamical fluctuations in multiparticle production induced by $^{16}$O nuclei at relativistic energy
paper.abstract_en: A detailed investigation of dynamical fluctuations in multiparticle production is carried out using the normalized factorial moment (NFM) technique for $^{16}$O-AgBr interactions at an incident energy of 60A GeV. The analysis reveals clear signatures of self-similar dynamical fluctuations in multiparticle production. However, the value of scaling exponent $\nu $ indicates that these fluctuations are of non-critical origin. Target excitation dependence of fluctuation phenomena is also studied by separating the experimental dataset into two parts depending on the emitted number of target recoil protons and it is observed that scaling exponent $\nu $ decrease with the increase in target excitation. The influence of initial-state nuclear structure on the observed fluctuations is further examined by incorporating alpha-cluster formation in the $^{16}$O nucleus within the AMPT simulation framework. Indications of alpha clustering are observed by the data.
